reason: Both correctly centred on overheating protection linked to the new drawer unit, but Conversation 2 escalated to the right party (the fitter who installed the drawer, plus Samsung support for warranty if it proves to be a hob fault), gave a practical way to capture the fleeting code (film the display), and offered sensible no-DIY workarounds when the homeowner refused to pull drawers out. Conversation 1 pushed an irrelevant 'suitable replacement' model-number panel for a hob, never suggested recalling the installer, and in its final turn drifted toward speculating the fan 'may have failed' and 'needs replacing' despite no evidence beyond a loud fan. Conversation 2's 'that pretty much nails it' was somewhat overconfident given the genuine fan/board uncertainty, and its first reply was overlong, but it still served the homeowner better on diagnosis, escalation and actionable advice.
